git.source_digest_rule: sha256 over name+bytes of src/trading_bot/research/edge01/*.py, scripts/edge01_run.py and scripts/edge01_verify.py, with CRLF folded to LF so the digest does not depend on the checkout's line endings

mode: deterministic backtest over the local historical corpus: DEV as the reference, VAL and OOS read once with the frozen ruleset; 0 orders, 0 credentials, 0 network calls

experiment.question: EDGE-TREND-01 4h is positive on DEV (+1,921.1792 USDT) and positive on OOS, but H3 warned that the OOS net may be one fat trade rather than an edge. Is there enough out-of-sample evidence — per asset, per calendar period, per regime and against buy & hold, before and after cost stress — to justify taking this ruleset to PAPER?

decision_rule.periods_are: calendar halves of the OOS window, declared before the run

meaning.SUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_FOR_PAPER: every requirement above met on OOS, plus the WP gate
meaning.NOT_SUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: the sample is powered and at least one requirement fails
meaning.UNPOWERED: fewer than the declared minimum OOS trades: nothing is concluded

decision_rule.not_claimed: PAPER here means the evidence supports wiring the frozen ruleset into the paper pipeline; it is not a profitability claim, not a live-trading authorisation and not a certification. No capital is at risk in this experiment.

wp_admission_criteria.note: Initial thresholds for WP-EDGE-01, recorded before the campaign ran. They are NOT an approved profitability bar; they are the minimum evidence needed to avoid calling noise an edge. The cost-stress criterion (OOS net still positive at 2x fees) is stated here rather than inferred from the measured results.

market_context.timeframe: 1d (aggregated from 1h shards; a day exists only when its 24 contiguous hours do)
market_context.rule: benchmark BTC daily close against its own 200-day EMA, with that EMA's 20-day change deciding trend from range: BULL when close > EMA200 and the EMA rose over the last 20 days, BEAR when close < EMA200 and it fell, SIDEWAYS otherwise, UNDEFINED while either input is still warming up. This is the project's existing convention (trading_bot/research/swing/backtest.py::build_regimes), reused rather than re-invented; it is a market label for reporting, never a signal.

reasons: no_single_trade_carries_the_net: largest trade is 0.7987 of the OOS net (limit 0.5)

limitations: the ruleset is untuned and frozen: VAL and OOS were read for it in the WP campaign already, so the OOS numbers here are a decomposition of the published run, not a second independent sample

the candidate risks a fixed share of equity per trade and caps the order notional, while buy & hold is fully invested in one asset: the comparison is on the same window and cost plane, not on the same capital utilisation
the periods are calendar halves declared here; three periods over fourteen months is a decomposition, not a statistical test
the 4h corpus is aggregated from 1h and ends 2026-02-28, so the last OOS stretch is shorter than a full half-year and no bar exists after that date
long side only (spot); no historical order book; nothing is wired into PAPER

combined.by_regime_note: entry trend state of the candidate's own filter (the value that let the trade through), NOT a market regime; see by_market_context for the benchmark-relative one
